name: KPSC / KAS (Karnataka)
description: Karnataka-focused questions for KPSC / KAS: state history, geography, polity and culture.

questions.question: What is the capital of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru has been the capital of Karnataka (earlier Mysore State) since 1956.

questions.question: The famous temples of Belur and Halebidu were built by which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Hoysalas (10th–14th century) built the star-shaped Chennakeshava (Belur) and Hoysaleshwara (Halebidu) temples — masterpieces of soapstone carving.

questions.question: The Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru is the seat of which institution?
questions.explanation: The Vidhana Soudha houses the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council. Built by Kengal Hanumanthaiah, it was completed in 1956.

questions.question: Who was the first Chief Minister of Karnataka (then Mysore State)?
questions.explanation: K. Chengalaraya (K. C.) Reddy became the first Chief Minister of Mysore State in 1947, after independence.

questions.question: The river Kaveri originates from which place in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Kaveri rises at Talakaveri on the Brahmagiri hills in Kodagu district and flows ~800 km to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Jog Falls, one of India's highest waterfalls, is formed by which river?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls (253 m) in Shivamogga district is formed by the Sharavati river plunging in four cascades — Raja, Rani, Rover and Rocket.

questions.question: Rani Chennamma of Kittur led an armed rebellion in 1824 against whom?
questions.explanation: Kittur Rani Chennamma fought the British East India Company in 1824 against the Doctrine of Lapse annexation — decades before the 1857 revolt.

questions.question: The world-famous Dasara (Nadahabba) festival is celebrated most grandly in which Karnataka city?
questions.explanation: Mysuru Dasara, a 10-day royal festival with the Jamboo Savari procession, has been celebrated for over 400 years under the Wodeyars.

questions.question: What is the official language of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kannada is Karnataka's official language — one of India's classical languages, with over 2,000 years of literary history.

questions.question: Which Karnataka district is most famous for coffee plantations?
questions.explanation: Kodagu (Coorg) is Karnataka's largest coffee-producing district; the state grows ~70% of India's coffee.

questions.question: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by whom?
options: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I
questions.explanation: Brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I founded the empire in 1336 on the banks of the Tungabhadra, guided by saint Vidyaranya.

questions.question: The UNESCO World Heritage ruins of Hampi lie on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, stands on the Tungabhadra river in Vijayanagara district.

questions.question: 'Kavirajamarga', the earliest available Kannada literary work, was composed during the reign of which Rashtrakuta king?
questions.explanation: Written by the poet Srivijaya around 850 CE in the court of Amoghavarsha I (Nrupatunga), 'Kavirajamarga' is a treatise on poetics.

questions.question: Bengaluru city was founded in 1537 by which chieftain?
questions.explanation: Kempe Gowda I, a feudatory of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded Bengaluru in 1537, building its mud fort and petes.

questions.question: Tipu Sultan, the 'Tiger of Mysore', was the ruler of which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan ruled the Kingdom of Mysore (1782–1799) and died defending Srirangapatna in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

questions.question: Which Karnataka city houses the state's major seaport — the New Mangalore Port?
questions.explanation: New Mangalore Port at Panambur (Mangaluru) is Karnataka's only major port, handling coffee, cashew and crude oil trade.

questions.question: The Gol Gumbaz, famous for its whispering gallery, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: Gol Gumbaz in Vijayapura is the mausoleum of Adil Shahi Sultan Mohammed Adil Shah — its dome is among the largest in the world.

questions.question: Karnataka was formed on 1 November 1956. What was the state called before it was renamed in 1973?
questions.explanation: The state was created as Mysore State on 1 November 1956 and renamed Karnataka on 1 November 1973 — now celebrated as Kannada Rajyotsava.

questions.question: Which is the highest peak in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Mullayyanagiri (1,930 m) in the Baba Budangiri range of Chikkamagaluru district is Karnataka's highest peak.

questions.question: The Halmidi inscription (~450 CE) is famous as what?
options: The earliest Sanskrit work of Karnataka
questions.explanation: Found in Hassan district, the Halmidi inscription is the earliest known full-length Kannada inscription, dating to about 450 CE.

questions.question: The Chennakeshava Temple at Belur (1117 CE) was commissioned during the reign of which Hoysala king?
questions.explanation: King Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur in 1117 CE to commemorate his victory over the Cholas at Talakad.

questions.question: Who was the Maharaja of Mysore when the state acceded to the Indian Union in 1947?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar signed the Instrument of Accession in 1947 and later served as Governor of Madras and Mysore.

questions.question: Which is the largest district of Karnataka by area?
questions.explanation: Belagavi (~13,415 km²) is Karnataka's largest district by area, in the state's northwest bordering Maharashtra and Goa.

questions.question: The Hampi ruins now fall under which district, carved out in 2020?
questions.explanation: Vijayanagara district (headquarters Hospete) was carved out of Ballari district in 2020, taking Hampi with it.

questions.question: Who is remembered as 'Karnataka Kulapurohita' — the high priest of the Karnataka unification movement?
questions.explanation: Aluru Venkata Rao's 1917 book 'Karnataka Gatha Vaibhava' inspired the Ekikarana (unification) movement, earning him the title Karnataka Kulapurohita.

questions.question: What is the state tree of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Sandalwood (Santalum album) is Karnataka's state tree — the state is famous for Mysore sandalwood. The state animal is the Asian Elephant.

questions.question: Kudremukh National Park is located in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kudremukh National Park (horse-face peak, 1,894 m) lies in Chikkamagaluru district in the Western Ghats — a UNESCO World Heritage cluster.

questions.question: The Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) dam near Mysuru is built across which river?
questions.explanation: The KRS dam, designed by Sir M. Visvesvaraya and completed in 1932, is built across the Kaveri and created the Brindavan Gardens.

questions.question: Which Kannada poet, author of 'Sri Ramayana Darshanam', is honoured as Karnataka's 'Rashtrakavi' (national poet)?
questions.explanation: Kuvempu (K. V. Puttappa) was the first Kannada Jnanpith awardee (1967) and was named Rashtrakavi; 'Jaya Bharata Jananiya Tanujate' is his anthem.

questions.question: Engineers' Day in India (15 September) honours which Karnataka-born engineer-statesman?
questions.explanation: Sir M. Visvesvaraya (born 15 Sept 1861, Muddenahalli) — KRS dam, Bharat Ratna 1955 — is honoured on Engineers' Day for his contributions.

questions.question: The Badami Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II is remembered for defeating which northern emperor on the Narmada?
questions.explanation: Pulakeshin II checked Harshavardhana's southward advance at the Narmada, an event recorded in the Aihole inscription. Harsha's expansion stopped there.

questions.question: The Aihole inscription, praising Pulakeshin II, was composed by which court poet?
questions.explanation: Ravikirti composed the Aihole prashasti in Sanskrit. Harisena wrote the comparable Allahabad pillar inscription for Samudragupta, and Pampa and Ranna were later Kannada poets.

questions.question: The Rashtrakuta dynasty ruled from which capital?
questions.explanation: The Rashtrakutas ruled from Manyakheta, modern Malkhed in Kalaburagi district. Badami was the Chalukya capital, Dwarasamudra the Hoysala one and Hampi the Vijayanagara one.

questions.question: The Kailasa temple at Ellora, carved from a single rock, was built under which dynasty of Karnataka origin?
questions.explanation: The Rashtrakuta king Krishna I commissioned the monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora. The Hoysalas built in soapstone much later and further south.

questions.question: The Kadamba dynasty, among the earliest to rule from Karnataka, had its capital at
questions.explanation: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada was the Kadamba capital, founded by Mayurasharma. Talakadu was a Western Ganga centre and Halebidu the Hoysala capital.

questions.question: The colossal Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola was commissioned by
questions.explanation: Chavundaraya, a Western Ganga minister and commander, had the monolith of Bahubali carved around 981 CE. Vishnuvardhana was a later Hoysala king.

questions.question: Krishnadevaraya, the best-known Vijayanagara emperor, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty, the third of the four Vijayanagara lines. Sangama was the founding dynasty and Aravidu the last.

questions.question: The Battle of Talikota in 1565, which broke Vijayanagara power, was fought against
questions.explanation: An alliance of the Deccan Sultanates defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota, after which Hampi was sacked. The Mughals had not yet reached the Deccan in force.

questions.question: Hyder Ali rose to power in Mysore as a commander under which ruling house?
questions.explanation: Hyder Ali served the Wadiyar rulers of Mysore before taking effective control of the kingdom. His son Tipu Sultan succeeded him.

questions.question: Onake Obavva is remembered for defending which fort against Hyder Ali's forces?
questions.explanation: Onake Obavva defended a narrow opening in the Chitradurga fort wall using a pestle. The fort is known for its seven concentric walls.

questions.question: The Keladi or Nayaka rulers of Ikkeri are associated with which region of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Keladi Nayakas ruled the Malnad and coastal tract from Ikkeri and later Bidnur. Queen Chennamma of Keladi famously sheltered Rajaram from the Mughals.

questions.question: The Ekikarana movement in Karnataka campaigned for what?
options: Unification of Kannada-speaking areas into one state
questions.explanation: Ekikarana was the movement to bring Kannada-speaking regions, then scattered across several administrations, into a single state, achieved in 1956.

questions.question: Which is the largest river basin in Karnataka by area within the state?
questions.explanation: The Krishna basin covers the largest share of Karnataka, draining the northern districts. The Kaveri basin dominates the south.

questions.question: The Tungabhadra river is formed by the confluence of the Tunga and Bhadra near which town?
questions.explanation: The Tunga and Bhadra meet at Koodli in Shivamogga district to form the Tungabhadra, a major tributary of the Krishna.

questions.question: Which Karnataka region is known as the Malnad?
questions.explanation: Malnad means hill country and refers to the Western Ghats belt of high rainfall and dense forest. The coastal strip is Karavali and the interior plateau Bayaluseeme.

questions.question: Karnataka's coastal region is commonly known as
questions.explanation: Karavali is the coastal belt covering Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada. Malnad is the hill country inland of it.

questions.question: The Kolar region of Karnataka was historically famous for mining which mineral?
questions.explanation: The Kolar Gold Fields were among the deepest gold mines in the world before closing in 2001. Ballari and Chitradurga are the iron ore districts instead.

questions.question: The Sharavathi river drains into which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Sharavathi is a west-flowing river reaching the Arabian Sea near Honnavar, plunging over Jog Falls on the way. The Kaveri and Krishna flow east.

questions.question: Bandipur National Park, a tiger reserve in Karnataka, lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Bandipur lies in Chamarajanagar district, adjoining Nagarhole in Karnataka and Mudumalai in Tamil Nadu as part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

questions.question: Which Karnataka district is the leading producer of iron ore?
questions.explanation: Ballari is Karnataka's principal iron ore district, with Chitradurga and Tumakuru also significant. Kodagu and Mandya are agricultural districts.

questions.question: The Deccan plateau region of northern Karnataka is drained mainly by which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Krishna and its tributary the Bhima drain the northern Karnataka plateau. The Netravati and Gurupura are short coastal rivers near Mangaluru.

questions.question: Who is the constitutional head of the state of Karnataka?
options: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.explanation: The Governor is the constitutional head of a state, appointed by the President, while the Chief Minister heads the elected government and exercises real executive power.

questions.question: The High Court of Karnataka has its principal seat at which city?
questions.explanation: The principal seat is at Bengaluru, with permanent benches at Dharwad and Kalaburagi to serve the northern districts.

questions.question: How many seats does Karnataka have in the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Karnataka elects 28 members to the Lok Sabha and has 12 Rajya Sabha seats, reflecting its population share.

questions.question: The Karnataka Lokayukta is an institution established to investigate
options: Corruption and maladministration by public servants
questions.explanation: The Lokayukta inquires into allegations of corruption and maladministration against public servants. Water disputes go to tribunals constituted under central law.

questions.question: The Kaveri water dispute primarily involves Karnataka and which other state?
questions.explanation: The long-running Kaveri dispute is chiefly between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, with Kerala and Puducherry also parties. The Krishna dispute involves Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh instead.

questions.question: Yakshagana, a traditional dance-drama, belongs chiefly to which part of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana is performed mainly in the coastal and Malnad districts, combining dance, music and elaborate costume to tell epic stories.

questions.question: The Vachana literary tradition of Kannada is associated with which twelfth-century reform movement?
questions.explanation: Vachanas are terse prose-poems by Basavanna and other sharanas of the Lingayat movement, rejecting caste and ritual. They are a landmark of Kannada literature.

questions.question: Basavanna, the social reformer and Vachana poet, served as a minister in whose court?
questions.explanation: Basavanna was a minister in the court of the Kalachuri king Bijjala at Kalyana. Vishnuvardhana was an earlier Hoysala ruler.

questions.question: How many Kannada writers have received the Jnanpith Award, the highest literary honour in India?
questions.explanation: Kannada has eight Jnanpith laureates, the joint highest for any Indian language, beginning with K. V. Puttappa and including Masti, Bendre and U. R. Ananthamurthy.

questions.question: Purandara Dasa, born in Karnataka, is revered as the father of which musical tradition?
questions.explanation: Purandara Dasa systematised the teaching of Carnatic music and is called its Pitamaha. He composed extensively in Kannada as part of the Haridasa movement.

questions.question: Bhimsen Joshi, the Hindustani vocalist born in Karnataka, belonged to which gharana?
questions.explanation: Bhimsen Joshi was the foremost exponent of the Kirana gharana and received the Bharat Ratna in 2008.

questions.question: Bengaluru is known as the Silicon Valley of India chiefly because of which industry?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is India's largest IT export centre, hosting software and services firms alongside aerospace and defence research establishments.

questions.question: Which crop is Karnataka the largest producer of in India?
questions.explanation: Karnataka produces the bulk of India's coffee, centred on Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan. Wheat and jute belong to the northern and eastern states.

questions.question: Karnataka is India's leading producer of which mineral used in the aerospace industry?
questions.explanation: Karnataka leads India in gold production, with Hutti in Raichur district the main working mine. India has no significant petroleum output from the state.

questions.question: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, India's main aircraft manufacturer, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: HAL is headquartered at Bengaluru, though it operates divisions at Nashik, Kanpur and elsewhere.

questions.question: Nagarhole National Park is also known by which name?
questions.explanation: Nagarhole is officially the Rajiv Gandhi National Park, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve alongside Bandipur.

questions.question: What is the state animal of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Indian elephant is the state animal and the Indian roller the state bird. Karnataka holds one of India's largest wild elephant populations.

questions.question: Ranganathittu, a well-known bird sanctuary in Karnataka, lies on which river?
questions.explanation: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary sits on islets in the Kaveri near Srirangapatna in Mandya district.

questions.question: The Western Ghats were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site primarily for which value?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats were listed for their exceptional biodiversity and high levels of endemism, being one of the world's recognised hotspots.
